principles: Dense global physical data loads on demand through tiles or provider services.
Physical hydrology is independent from sacred or textual river overlays.
Bare or sparse vegetation is not synonymous with desert or aridity.

entries.label: Terrain
entries.status_note: Elevation and hillshade load only after explicit activation. Provider failure is nonfatal.

entries.label: Water

source.dataset: 1:110m world overview + 1:50m regional-detail coastline, lakes, rivers and lake centerlines
source.attribution: Made with Natural Earth · public domain

entries.status_note: Scale-adaptive cartographic water context: 1:110m at world scale and lazily loaded 1:50m detail at regional zoom. It is not a legal boundary or drainage-basin authority layer.

entries.label: Hydrology
entries.status_note: Measured physical drainage context. It remains independent from Eden/Four-Rivers sacred or textual overlays.

entries.label: Land cover

source.dataset: WorldCover 2021 global land-cover map at 10 m
source.attribution: © ESA WorldCover project 2021 / Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data (2021) processed by ESA WorldCover consortium

entries.status_note: Visual land-cover context from the official cached WorldCover web map service. Classes include trees, shrubland, grassland, cropland, built-up, bare/sparse vegetation, water, wetland, mangroves, moss/lichen and snow/ice. Bare/sparse vegetation is not the same thing as desert. The RGB web layer is cartographic context, not an analytical class-query service.

entries.label: Deserts / xeric

source.dataset: Global Terrestrial Ecoregions · Deserts and Xeric Shrublands

entries.status_note: Ecological ecoregion context for Deserts and Xeric Shrublands. This is a dated 2009 terrestrial ecoregion classification, not a continuous aridity index, not current desert extent, and not equivalent to WorldCover bare/sparse vegetation.
